rationale: This benchmark is a template-heavy, abstraction-penalizing workload (stepanov_abstraction) whose 19 functions are dominated by a single large main (~8.5KB of ~13.9KB text) running tight, timer-measured loops (heapsort, vector abstractions, constant-folding and loop-invariant kernels), so the weighting strongly prioritizes transformations with high static-analysis resistance per unit of dynamic overhead: SUB gets the highest application pressure because it hardens the arithmetic-dense kernels at near-zero runtime and size cost, and FLA is weighted heavily because flattening the large main and the big sort routines destroys the structural control-flow signatures that reverse engineers rely on most, while its dispatcher overhead is tolerable outside the hottest inner loops; BCF is enabled at moderate weight with elevated size/runtime penalties since its code-bloat multiplies quickly in a 13.9KB binary whose few large functions would absorb most of it; SPLIT is kept as a cheap diversity booster to break up basic-block matching across the many small template instantiations (the three heapsort variants) without meaningful cost; and IBR, ICALL, and IGV are held at low weight with high runtime/correctness penalties because indirect branch and call dispatch directly tax the branch-predictor-sensitive hot loops this benchmark exists to measure, indirect calls interact hazardously with C++ template instantiations and exception paths, and the program has little global-variable surface for IGV to protect — the cost/risk dimensions are weighted so only passes whose per-function features show genuinely low dynamic impact in these hot paths will still be selected.
